newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-FOURTH SUCCESSIVE EUROPEAN TITLE IN MONTGOMERIE'S GRASP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FOURTH SUCCESSIVE EUROPEAN TITLE IN MONTGOMERIE'S GRASP.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie became virtually certain of being European number one for the fourth successive year after his only challenger Ian Woosnam missed the halfway cut at the German Masters on Friday.
The burly Scot shot a second round 67 for a halfway aggregate of 137. He is four shots behind leader Paul McGinley of Ireland who is 11 under par after also hitting a 67.
Woosnam, who had a 75 for a level par 144 and missed the cut by one shot, was in no doubt that his last chance of catching Montgomerie had gone.
The 38-year-old Welshman, who said it was his "shocking putting" and not his troublesome back that was to blame for his poor score, remarked: "Well, that's it. It's all over. I can go home now."

Technically Woosnam is still in the race but only just. Montgomerie is 143,347 pounds ($223,621) ahead of the Welshman in the rankings and has only to finish in the top 40 in Berlin on Sunday to win enough prize money to be out of reach.

It will not matter then what happens when they both play in the last counting event, the Volvo Masters at Valderrama, later this month. It means Montgomerie is on the verge of equalling the record of Peter Oosterhuis, who was also European number one four years running, from 1971 to 1974.

While the race at the top of the money list was almost completed, the three Irishmen, McGinley, Darren Clarke and Padraig Harrington, who will represent their country in the Dunhill Cup at St Andrews next week, were all in top form.
McGinley is the outright leader, Clarke fired an eight under par 64 to share joint second with England's Paul Eales on 134 and Harrington claimed a share of fourth place on 135 after shooting 67.
Clarke, who had an almost flawless round of six birdies and one eagle in his 64, said: "It's great we are all playing well and it could be a good week for us at St Andrews."
